name: Question 7
problem:
Select the correct options in the truth table below and use this to determine whether $(¬X∨Y)∧(X∧Y)$ is a contradiction.

| $\,X\,$ | $\,Y\,$ | $\,¬X∨Y\,$ | $\,X∧Y\,$ | $\,(¬X∨Y)∧(X∧Y)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-1}} |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-2}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-3}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-4}} |

According to the table, $(¬X∨Y)∧(X∧Y)$ 
{{field-5}}
always false. Therefore, it 
{{field-6}} 
a contradiction.
worked_solution:
An expression is a contradiction if it is always false, regardless of the inputs.

By completing the final column in the truth table below, we obtain the following:

| $\,X\,$ | $\,Y\,$ | $\,¬X∨Y\,$ | $\,X∧Y\,$ | $\,(¬X∨Y)∧(X∧Y)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |

According to the table, $(¬X∨Y)∧(X∧Y)$ 
$\text{isn't}$
always false. Therefore, it 
$\text{isn't}$
a contradiction.
